correctness.rationale: For a two-digit candidate N=(a,c)_b, ac|(ab+c) forces a|c. Writing c=ak gives the equivalent condition ak|(b+k), hence k|b. With d=b/k this is exactly a|(d+1), while the digit bound is a<d. Proper divisors of d+1 automatically satisfy a<d for d>=2. The inverse reconstruction k=c/a and d=b/k proves a bijection. The lower bound and equality classification then follow from elementary divisor and parity arguments. A fresh exhaustive checker agrees for every base 2 through 500.

value.rationale: Exact digit-length counts are a stated computational target in modern Zuckerman-number research. The result closes the first nontrivial length for every base with a bijective divisor-lattice formula, rather than a bounded census. It also yields a sharp structural lower bound whose equality case is completely classified, and a simple prime-base specialization.
